heading.found: dang po skyes bu chung du dang thun mong ba'i lam gyi rim par blo sbyang ba ni
heading.expected: dang po skyes bu chung ngu dang thun mong ba'i lam gyi rim par blo sbyang ba ni
heading.evidence: The Lam Rim scope idiom is 'skyes bu chung ngu' (person of lesser capacity); 'chung du' is not parsable here, since a terminative du cannot feed the comitative dang that follows. FILED AGAINST PROPOSAL B, WHICH REJECTED IT — B's counter-evidence does not survive checking. (1) Same-course parallel: C03:225 is the outline heading for this very section and reads 'skyes bu chung ngu dang thun mong ba'i lam gyi rim par blo sbyang ba' — identical to this clause word-for-word, including the distinctive 'rim par' (other witnesses read 'rim pa la'), differing ONLY in ngu/du. Its ACIP reads 'SKYES BU CHUNG NGU DANG ... RIM PAR BLO SBYANG BA,'. C03:401, the section header, glosses it 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'. (2) Counts: 'skyes bu chung ngu' occurs in 23 spine segments (C02:40, C08:309, C09:214, C09:216, C16:238, C17:402, TCS01:223, TCS01:317, TCS01:318, TCS03:20, SSL:107, SSL:111, SSL:395, ...); 'skyes bu chung du' occurs in exactly 2 — this segment and TCS18Commentary:322, a different text and not a parallel of this passage. (3) B's claim that 'chung du' is 'a live adverbial form' across TCS03/05/06/09/10/11/15/16 is a category error. I enumerated every 'chung du' in the spine with context: TCS03:446 'chung du song', TCS05:499 'mthu chung du gtang', TCS06:161 'chung du 'gro', TCS06:341 'chung chung du gnas', TCS07:681 'chung du 'gro', TCS09:501 'chung du 'gro', TCS10:322/418 'je chung je chung du bsdus/song', TCS10:323/405, TCS11:265/333, TCS15:448 'drod chung du 'gro', TCS16Reading:159, EM:956, EM:1126, C01:105 — every one is adverbial terminative du plus a verb of diminution ('become/make smaller'), a wholly different construction. Not one is the skyes-bu scope idiom. The string 'chung du dang' occurs exactly twice in the entire spine: this segment and TCS18Commentary:322. The true adverbial du never once feeds a comitative dang. (4) B read the ACIP apparatus backwards. In ACIP, {%X} is the EDITORS' CORRECTION, so GIE:650 "chung du'i {%ngu'i} chung du {%ngu}" is evidence that du-for-ngu IS an error, not that it is accepted; the same correction recurs at AK:156 'chung du {%ngu%}', AK:842 'chung dur {%ngur}', GK:97 'chung dus {%ngus}', SOS:25 'chung dus {%ngus}'. This is a documented, editor-corrected keying slip class. (5) The ACIP field of this same segment also reads 'CHUNG DU', so the slip is in the keyed source, not introduced by the wylie transliteration step. Span s402-21 preserves 'chung du' byte-for-byte per rule 1.

heading.expected: THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I GO 'PHANG BSGRUB PA
heading.evidence: Confirmed from this segment's own text. ACIP (source of record) reads GO 'PANG; the wylie field carries the same reading, go 'pang, so this is in the source, not the converter. The word is go 'phang (rank, station, state), which is what GMR translates: 'the state of All-Knowing'. Re-derived corpus counts: acip LIKE '%GO ''PANG%' returns exactly one row, C03:445; acip LIKE '%GO ''PHANG%' returns 219; the wylie field splits identically, 1 vs 219. Stronger still, the syllable 'pang occurs NOWHERE else in the corpus wylie: a-chung ('a) prefixes only voiced or aspirated radicals in Tibetan orthography ('g 'j 'd 'b 'dz 'kh 'ch 'th 'ph 'tsh), so 'p- is not a spellable syllable onset and 'pang cannot be a variant. Parallel-witness check: no other segment carries this passage (english LIKE '%habit of hoping for the%', english LIKE '%up to the final end%', wylie LIKE '%tshe ''di snang gi zhen pa%', wylie LIKE '%rang res ngan ''gro%' each return C03:445 alone). The exact collocation mkhyen pa'i go 'p… appears in seven other rows, every one of them 'phang: C01:84, C16:32, TCS02:315, TCS09:37, Sunlight:595, Sunlight:707, SPF:461. The nearest relative for the surrounding idiom, ILL:126 (thog mtha' bar gsum du gal che), shares only that closing idiom and says nothing about go 'phang. Registered classes checked and not applicable: no {SHl} drop, no fused footnote number, no folio marker, no glued heading; the ACIP trailing shad ',' absent from the wylie is the normal strip, and ACIP TSE for wylie tshe is the ACIP convention (TS = tsh), not an error. A dropped aspiration H in one row against 219 correct ones, yielding an impossible syllable, is a keystroke error.

The local C05ReadingASCII.txt also reads 'In the hells through' on line 1553, so this is present in the source reading, not introduced by corpus ingestion; that file is the same source, not an independent witness. The source Tibetan adversative is 'on kyang (ACIP 'ON KYANG). Its HGM glossary-tier HTG2016 entry includes though, nonetheless, however and but. In this sentence through has no complement and cannot function as that adversative, whereas though supplies the contrast between four projections generally and only three virtuous projections in the hells.
